content.title: Rand Paul presses Mullin on past assault remarks
content.text: Skip to contentHomeNewsSportBusinessTechnologyHealthCultureArtsTravelEarthAudioVideoLiveDocumentariesWeatherNewslettersWatch Live0:55Rand Paul presses Mullin on past assault remarksKentucky Senator Rand Paul, who leads the Senate Committee on Homeland Security, spoke about political violence in his opening remarks, including an attack Paul himself faced where he had six of his ribs broken by a neighbour in 2017.Paul questioned if someone who applauds political violence is the right person to lead the Department of Homeland Security, while offering President Donald Trump's pick to become the new leader of the Department of Homeland Security, Senator MarkWayne Mullin, the chance to apologise for reportedly previously saying he understood why a neighbour attacked Paul, a Republican.18 March 2026United StatesShareSaveExplore More'A historical moment' - Americans react to birthright citizenship caseSuited up and ready to go: Watch the Artemis crew's journey to launch'Something needs to be done' - Americans struggle as petrol prices surgeAs Iran war continues, US farmers absorb rising costs'Art is a very powerful tool' - Golden toilet throne appears in DCHow will the Artemis astronauts go to the toilet in space?Behind the scenes: Astronaut training for Nasa’s moon missionInside Nasa's moon spacesuit lab ahead of Artemis launch'No Kings' protesters gather across the US as Bruce Springsteen joins rallyExpectant mothers in Cuba struggle under fuel blockadeOne month in, what do American conservatives make of the war in Iran?BBC journalist caught in travel chaos at Houston Airport'Affordability is the biggest thing' - Conservatives mixed on economy under TrumpWhat happened at Maduro's second court appearanceIs social media addictive?
